title: Aggregate Functions in SQL
definition: Aggregate functions perform calculations on multiple rows of a table and return a single value.

count_function.heading: COUNT Function
count_function.definition: COUNT returns the total number of rows that match a specified condition.
queries: SELECT COUNT(emp_id) FROM employee WHERE dept = 'IT';

sum_function.heading: SUM Function
sum_function.definition: SUM returns the total value of a numeric column.
queries: SELECT SUM(salary) FROM employee WHERE dept = 'IT';

avg_function.heading: AVG Function
avg_function.definition: AVG returns the average value of a numeric column.
queries: SELECT AVG(salary) FROM employee WHERE dept = 'HR';
SELECT AVG(salary) FROM employee WHERE city = 'Delhi';

min_max_function.heading: MIN and MAX Functions
min_max_function.definition: MIN returns the smallest value and MAX returns the largest value in a column.

group_by_clause.heading: GROUP BY Clause
group_by_clause.definition: GROUP BY groups rows that have the same values so that aggregate functions can be applied on each group.
queries: SELECT dept FROM employee GROUP BY dept;
SELECT dept, COUNT(emp_id) FROM employee GROUP BY dept;
SELECT dept, SUM(salary) FROM employee GROUP BY dept;
SELECT city, AVG(salary) FROM employee GROUP BY city;

queries_with_output.query: SELECT dept, COUNT(emp_id) FROM employee GROUP BY dept;
SELECT dept, AVG(salary) FROM employee GROUP BY dept;
